Concept: Angles on a straight line add up to 180° (they are supplementary).
Step 1: From the diagram, the two angles sit side by side on one straight line. One is 115° and the other is the unknown.
Step 2: Write the equation: 115° + unknown = 180°.
Step 3: Subtract: 180° − 115° = 65°.
Answer: 65°
Common mistake: Using 360° (angles round a point) instead of 180° (angles on a line) gives 245°, which is wrong here.
Similar example: Two angles on a straight line: one is 135°. The other is 180° − 135° = 45°.
Tip: Straight line means 180°. Full turn around a point means 360°.

questions.text: In the isosceles triangle shown, AB = AC and the base angles are each 40°. Find the angle at the vertex A.

questions.text: The triangle PQR shown is right-angled at Q, with PQ = 3 cm and QR = 4 cm. Find PR.
questions.explanation:
Concept: In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse (the longest side, opposite the right angle) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
Step 1: From the diagram, the two shorter sides are 3 cm and 4 cm.
Step 2: Square and add: 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25.
Step 3: Take the square root: PR = √25 = 5 cm.
Answer: 5 cm
Common mistake: Adding the sides (3 + 4 = 7) instead of squaring them first, or forgetting the final square root and answering 25.
Similar example: Sides 9 cm and 12 cm give hypotenuse √(81 + 144) = √225 = 15 cm.
Tip: Learn the common triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 6-8-10.

questions.text: In the right-angled triangle shown, the hypotenuse is 13 cm and one other side is 5 cm. Find the third side.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Pythagoras' theorem can be rearranged to find a shorter side: (shorter side)² = (hypotenuse)² − (other side)².
Step 1: From the diagram, the hypotenuse is 13 cm and one shorter side is 5 cm.
Step 2: Square and subtract: 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144.
Step 3: Take the square root: √144 = 12 cm.
Answer: 12 cm
Common mistake: Adding the squares (194) when the missing side is a shorter side. You only add the squares when you are finding the hypotenuse.
Similar example: Hypotenuse 25 cm and one side 7 cm: other side = √(625 − 49) = √576 = 24 cm.
Tip: The hypotenuse is always the longest side. If your answer for a shorter side is bigger than the hypotenuse, you added instead of subtracted.

questions.text: The rectangle shown measures 9 cm by 12 cm. Find the length of its diagonal.

Step 3: Take the square root: diagonal = √225 = 15 cm.
Answer: 15 cm
Common mistake: Adding the two sides (9 + 12 = 21). A diagonal is a straight shortcut, so it is shorter than going along two sides.
Similar example: A rectangle 15 cm by 20 cm has diagonal √(225 + 400) = √625 = 25 cm.
Tip: The diagonal is always shorter than length + width but longer than either side.

questions.text: In the diagram, O is the centre of the circle and angle AOB = 80°. Find angle APB.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The angle at the centre of a circle is twice the angle at the circumference when both stand on the same arc.
Step 1: From the diagram, O is the centre and angle AOB = 80° stands on arc AB. Angle APB, at point P on the circumference, stands on the same arc.
Step 2: Angle at circumference = ½ × angle at centre.
Step 3: Angle APB = ½ × 80° = 40°.
Answer: 40°
Common mistake: Doubling instead of halving (160°). The angle at the circumference is always the smaller one.
Similar example: Angle at the centre 120° means angle at the circumference 60°.
Tip: Centre is double, circumference is half. The smaller angle is at the circumference.

questions.text: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral. If angle SPQ = 80°, find angle QRS.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral (all four corners on a circle) add up to 180°.
Step 1: From the diagram, PQRS is cyclic and angle SPQ = 80°. Angle QRS is opposite to angle SPQ.
Step 2: Write: angle SPQ + angle QRS = 180°.
Step 3: angle QRS = 180° − 80° = 100°.
Answer: 100°
Common mistake: Using 360° (the total for all four angles) when you only need the pair of opposite angles, which add to 180°.
Similar example: In a cyclic quadrilateral, one angle is 95°. The opposite angle is 180° − 95° = 85°.
Tip: Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles are supplementary.

questions.text: Three angles of the quadrilateral shown are 80°, 95° and 105°. Find x.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The four interior angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360°.
Step 1: Read the three given angles from the diagram: 80°, 95° and 105°.
Step 2: Add them: 80 + 95 + 105 = 280°.
Step 3: Subtract from 360°: x = 360° − 280° = 80°.
Answer: 80°
Common mistake: Subtracting from 180° (the triangle total) gives -100°, which makes no sense here. A quadrilateral can be split into two triangles, so its total is 2 × 180° = 360°.
Similar example: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90°, 100° and 70°. The fourth is 360° − 260° = 100°.
Tip: Triangle 180°, quadrilateral 360°, pentagon 540°. Add 180° for each extra side.

questions.text: In the diagram, a = 65°. Find the value of b, given that the two horizontal lines are parallel.
questions.explanation:
Concept: When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, alternate angles are equal. Here a and b are alternate exterior angles (outside the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal).
Step 1: From the diagram, a lies above the top line on the left of the transversal, and b lies below the bottom line on the right.
Step 2: Because they are alternate exterior angles on parallel lines, b = a.
Step 3: b = 65°.
Answer: 65°
Common mistake: Writing 180° − 65° = 115°. That rule is for angles that form a straight line (a linear pair) or co-interior angles, not for alternate angles.
Similar example: If a = 72° and the lines are parallel, the alternate exterior angle is also 72°.
Tip: Alternate angles are equal (Z-shape). Co-interior angles add up to 180° (C-shape).

questions.text: In the diagram, a = 48°. Find the value of b, given that the two horizontal lines are parallel.

questions.text: In the diagram, the horizontal lines are parallel and a = 65°. Find c.
questions.explanation:
Concept: When a transversal cuts parallel lines, alternate exterior angles are equal, and angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
Step 1: From the diagram, a = 65°. The angle b (below the bottom line) is the alternate exterior angle of a, so b = 65°.
Step 2: Angles b and c lie next to each other on the straight line made by the bottom parallel line, so b + c = 180°.
Step 3: c = 180° − 65° = 115°.
Answer: 115°
Common mistake: Answering 65° because it "looks the same". c is next to b, not opposite, so it is the supplement, not the equal angle.
Similar example: If a = 50°, then b = 50° and c = 130°.
Tip: With parallel lines there are only two angle sizes: x and 180° − x.

questions.text: The tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact. In the diagram, OT is a radius and the line through T is a tangent. The angle between them is
questions.explanation:
Concept: A tangent to a circle touches it at exactly one point, and it is always perpendicular to the radius drawn to that point.
Step 1: From the diagram, OT is a radius and the line through T is a tangent. T is the point of contact.
Step 2: The radius to the point of contact meets the tangent at a right angle.
Answer: 90°
Common mistake: Choosing 180° (a straight line) or 45°. The tangent and the radius form a right angle, shown by the small square symbol in a correct diagram.

Tip: Whenever you see a tangent, draw the radius to the point of contact and mark 90°.

questions.text: Find the area of the trapezium shown with parallel sides 8 cm and 14 cm and height 6 cm.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. Its area is half the sum of the parallel sides multiplied by the distance between them: A = ½(a + b)h.
Step 1: From the diagram, the parallel sides are 8 cm and 14 cm, and the perpendicular height is 6 cm.
Step 2: Add the parallel sides: 8 + 14 = 22.
Step 3: Multiply by the height and halve: ½ × 22 × 6 = 66 cm².
Answer: 66 cm²
Common mistake: Forgetting the ½ gives 132 cm², which is double the correct area. Also, use the perpendicular height, not the slanting side.
Similar example: Parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm, height 4 cm: A = ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 cm².
Tip: Area = average of the parallel sides × height.

questions.text: The diagonals of the rhombus shown are 12 cm and 16 cm. Find its area.

Tip: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles, so the rhombus is made of four equal right-angled triangles.

Step 2: Multiply them: 8 × 6 = 48.
Step 3: Take half: ½ × 48 = 24 cm².
Answer: 24 cm²
Common mistake: Forgetting the ½ and answering 48 cm². That is the area of the rectangle drawn round the rhombus, which is twice as big.
Similar example: Diagonals 8 cm and 10 cm give an area of ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 cm².
Tip: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles, so the rhombus is made of four equal right-angled triangles.

questions.text: Find the volume of the cuboid shown.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A cuboid is a box shape. Its volume is length × width × height.
Step 1: Read the three edge lengths from the diagram: 8 cm, 3 cm and 5 cm.
Step 2: Multiply the first two: 8 × 3 = 24.
Step 3: Multiply by the third: 24 × 5 = 120.
Answer: 120 cm³
Common mistake: Adding the lengths (8 + 3 + 5 = 16) instead of multiplying them. Volume is always in cubic units (cm³).
Similar example: A cuboid 6 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm has volume 6 × 4 × 5 = 120 cm³.
Tip: Volume of any prism = area of the base × height.

questions.text: Find the total surface area of the cuboid shown.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces in 3 pairs. Total surface area = 2(lw + wh + lh).
Step 1: From the diagram, the edges are 8 cm, 3 cm and 5 cm.

Step 3: Add them: 24 + 15 + 40 = 79.
Step 4: Double it because each face has an identical partner: 2 × 79 = 158 cm².

Tip: Surface area is in cm², volume is in cm³.

questions.text: Find the volume of the cylinder shown. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
Concept: A cylinder is a circle stretched upward. Volume = (area of circle) × height = πr²h.
Step 1: Read from the diagram: radius r = 7 cm and height h = 10 cm. Use π = 22/7.
Step 2: Find the area of the base: πr² = (22/7) × 7² = (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm².
Step 3: Multiply by the height: 154 × 10 = 1540 cm³.
Answer: 1540 cm³
Common mistake: Forgetting to square the radius (using π × r × h), or using the diameter in place of the radius.
Similar example: r = 7 cm, h = 2 cm: V = (22/7) × 49 × 2 = 308 cm³.
Tip: Square the radius first, then multiply by π, then by the height.

questions.text: Find the curved surface area of the cylinder shown. (Take π = 22/7)

Step 2: Substitute: CSA = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 10.
Step 3: Cancel the 7 and multiply: 440 cm².

Common mistake: Using πr²h, which is the volume formula. Curved surface area has only ONE radius in it (and no flat circles are included).
Similar example: r = 7 cm, h = 3 cm: 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 3 = 132 cm².
Tip: CSA excludes the top and bottom circles. Adding them gives the total surface area: 2πrh + 2πr².

Step 2: Substitute: V = ⅓ × (22/7) × 3² × 4 = ⅓ × (22/7) × 36.

Similar example: r = 7 cm, h = 6 cm: V = ⅓ × (22/7) × 49 × 6 = 308 cm³.
Tip: Use the vertical height, not the slant height.

questions.text: Find the area of the sector shown. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
Concept: A sector is a slice of a circle. Its area is the fraction θ/360 of the whole circle's area: Area = (θ/360) × πr².
Step 1: From the diagram, θ = 90° and r = 6 cm. Use π = 22/7.
Step 2: Write the fraction of the circle: 90/360 = 1/4.
Step 3: Find the area of the whole circle: πr² = (22/7) × 6² = (22/7) × 36 = 792/7 cm².
Step 4: Multiply: 1/4 × 792/7 = 198/7 cm².
Answer: 198/7 ≈ 28.29 cm²
Common mistake: Giving the area of the whole circle (792/7 cm²). A sector is only part of the circle.
Similar example: A sector with r = 7 cm and angle 120°: (120/360) × (22/7) × 49 = (1/3) × 154 = 154/3 ≈ 51.33 cm².
Tip: Simplify θ/360 first, and cancel the 7 in 22/7 against r² when r is a multiple of 7.

questions.text: The bar chart shows the data collected. Which category has the highest value?
questions.explanation:
Concept: In a bar chart, the height of each bar shows its value, so the tallest bar is the highest value.
Step 1: Read each bar against the vertical scale: Mon = 20, Tue = 35, Wed = 25, Thu = 40, Fri = 30.
Step 2: Compare them. The largest value is 40.
Step 3: That value belongs to the bar labelled Thu.
Answer: Thu
Common mistake: Picking the first or last bar without checking. Always read every bar against the scale.
Similar example: Bars of 12, 18, 9 and 21 for A, B, C and D: the tallest bar is D (21).
Tip: Use the gridlines on the diagram. Run your finger straight across from the top of the bar to the scale.

questions.text: From the bar chart, find the total of all the bars.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To find the total from a bar chart, read every bar and add the values.
Step 1: Read each bar against the vertical scale: Mon = 20, Tue = 35, Wed = 25, Thu = 40, Fri = 30.
Step 2: Add them: 20 + 35 + 25 + 40 + 30 = 150.
Answer: 150
Common mistake: Reading one bar wrongly because the scale goes up in steps (not in ones), or leaving out a bar. Check that you used all 5 bars.
Similar example: Bars of 10, 20, 15 and 5 give a total of 50.
Tip: Add in pairs that make round numbers to avoid slips.

questions.text: What is the difference between the highest and the lowest values on the bar chart?
questions.explanation:
Concept: The difference between the highest and lowest values is the range of the data.
Step 1: Read each bar against the vertical scale: Mon = 20, Tue = 35, Wed = 25, Thu = 40, Fri = 30.
Step 2: Highest value = 40 (Thu). Lowest value = 20 (Mon).
Step 3: Subtract: 40 − 20 = 20.
Answer: 20
Common mistake: Subtracting the first bar from the last bar instead of the lowest from the highest.
Similar example: Highest 30 and lowest 12 give a difference of 18.
Tip: Always find the tallest and the shortest bar first, then subtract.

questions.text: In the pie chart shown, what percentage is represented by the largest sector?
questions.explanation:
Concept: In a pie chart, a sector's percentage is (angle ÷ 360°) × 100. The largest sector has the biggest angle.
Step 1: From the diagram, the angles are 90°, 120°, 60°, 90°. Check: they add up to 360°.
Step 2: The largest angle is 120°.
Step 3: Percentage = 120/360 × 100 = 100/3% ≈ 33.33%.
Answer: 33.3333%
Common mistake: Writing the fraction 1/3 as a percentage without multiplying by 100, or using the angle itself as the percentage.
Similar example: A sector of 150° out of 360° is 150/360 × 100 = 41⅔%.
Tip: 360° is 100%, so 1% = 3.6°.

questions.text: The pie chart shown represents 180 students. How many students are represented by the 90° sector?
questions.explanation:
Concept: A sector's share of the whole is its angle ÷ 360°. Multiply that fraction by the total to get the number of students.
Step 1: The whole pie chart represents 180 students and the sector in question has an angle of 90°.
Step 2: Fraction of the circle = 90/360 = 1/4.
Step 3: Number of students = 1/4 × 180 = 45.
Answer: 45 students
Common mistake: Choosing the angle itself (90) as the number of students. Angles are measured out of 360°, but the total here is 180 students, so you must scale.
Similar example: A 60° sector of a pie chart for 240 people: 60/360 × 240 = 40 people.
Tip: Students = (angle ÷ 360) × total.

Answer: 60 students
Common mistake: Choosing the angle itself (120) as the number of students. Angles are measured out of 360°, but the total here is 180 students, so you must scale.
Similar example: A 60° sector of a pie chart for 240 people: 60/360 × 240 = 40 people.
Tip: Students = (angle ÷ 360) × total.

questions.text: The histogram shows the distribution of marks. How many observations are there altogether?
questions.explanation:
Concept: In a histogram, the height of each bar is the frequency of its class. The total number of observations is the sum of all the frequencies.
Step 1: Read the frequency of each class from the diagram: 0-9: 5, 10-19: 12, 20-29: 18, 30-39: 10.
Step 2: Add: 5 + 12 + 18 + 10 = 45.
Answer: 45
Common mistake: Counting the bars (4) instead of adding their heights, or adding the class boundaries.
Similar example: Frequencies 3, 7, 9 and 1 give 20 observations in total.
Tip: Total frequency = Σf. Check with the vertical scale before adding.

questions.text: Which class interval is the modal class in the histogram?
questions.explanation:
Concept: The modal class is the class with the highest frequency, which is the tallest bar of the histogram.
Step 1: Read the frequency of each class: 0-9: 5, 10-19: 12, 20-29: 18, 30-39: 10.
Step 2: The highest frequency is 18.
Step 3: This belongs to the class 20-29.
Answer: 20-29
Common mistake: Giving the frequency (18) instead of the class interval. The question asks for the class.
Similar example: Frequencies 4, 9, 6 and 2 for classes 0–4, 5–9, 10–14 and 15–19: modal class 5–9.
Tip: Mode is about the most frequent, so look for the tallest bar.

questions.text: What fraction of the observations lie in the first two classes?
questions.explanation:
Concept: A fraction of the observations = (frequency in the classes asked for) ÷ (total frequency).
Step 1: Read the frequencies: 0-9: 5, 10-19: 12, 20-29: 18, 30-39: 10.
Step 2: First two classes: 5 + 12 = 17.
Step 3: Total of all classes: 5 + 12 + 18 + 10 = 45.
Step 4: Fraction = 17/45 = 17/45.
Answer: 17/45
Common mistake: Dividing by the number of classes (4) instead of the total frequency, or forgetting to simplify.
Similar example: Frequencies 2, 6, 8 and 4 (total 20): the first two classes make 8/20 = 2/5.
Tip: Part ÷ whole, then simplify.

Step 2: Add: 8 + 14 + 10 + 6 = 38.

Step 4: Fraction = 16/40 = 2/5.

questions.text: The shaded region in the diagram is bounded by the line y = 2x + 1, the x-axis, x = 0 and x = 3. Find its area.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The area under a curve between x = a and x = b is the definite integral ∫ y dx from a to b.
Step 1: From the diagram, the shaded region lies under y = 2x + 1 between x = 0 and x = 3.
Step 2: Integrate: ∫ (2x + 1) dx = x² + x.
Step 3: Substitute the limits: upper limit x = 3 gives 12, lower limit x = 0 gives 0.
Step 4: Subtract (upper − lower): 12 − 0 = 12.
Answer: 12 square units
Common mistake: Evaluating only at the upper limit. You must evaluate at BOTH limits and subtract (upper − lower).
Similar example: Area under y = 4x from x = 0 to x = 3: [2x²] = 18 − 0 = 18 square units.
Tip: For a straight line you can also check with the area of a trapezium or triangle.

questions.text: The shaded region in the diagram is bounded by the line y = x + 2, the x-axis, x = 1 and x = 4. Find its area.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The area under a curve between x = a and x = b is the definite integral ∫ y dx from a to b.
Step 1: From the diagram, the shaded region lies under y = x + 2 between x = 1 and x = 4.
Step 2: Integrate: ∫ (x + 2) dx = x²/2 + 2x.
Step 3: Substitute the limits: upper limit x = 4 gives 16, lower limit x = 1 gives 2.5.
Step 4: Subtract (upper − lower): 16 − 2.5 = 27/2.
Answer: 27/2 square units
Common mistake: Evaluating only at the upper limit. You must evaluate at BOTH limits and subtract (upper − lower).
Similar example: Area under y = 4x from x = 0 to x = 3: [2x²] = 18 − 0 = 18 square units.
Tip: For a straight line you can also check with the area of a trapezium or triangle.

questions.text: The shaded region in the diagram is bounded by the line y = 3x, the x-axis, x = 0 and x = 2. Find its area.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The area under a curve between x = a and x = b is the definite integral ∫ y dx from a to b.
Step 1: From the diagram, the shaded region lies under y = 3x between x = 0 and x = 2.
Step 2: Integrate: ∫ (3x) dx = 3x²/2.
Step 3: Substitute the limits: upper limit x = 2 gives 6, lower limit x = 0 gives 0.
Step 4: Subtract (upper − lower): 6 − 0 = 6.
Answer: 6 square units
Common mistake: Evaluating only at the upper limit. You must evaluate at BOTH limits and subtract (upper − lower).
Similar example: Area under y = 4x from x = 0 to x = 3: [2x²] = 18 − 0 = 18 square units.
Tip: For a straight line you can also check with the area of a trapezium or triangle.

questions.text: The diagram shows part of the curve y = x². Find the area of the shaded region between x = 0 and x = 2.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The area under y = x² between two x-values is found by integrating: ∫x² dx = x³/3.
Step 1: From the diagram, the shaded region lies under y = x² between x = 0 and x = 2.
Step 2: Integrate: ∫ x² dx = x³/3.
Step 3: Substitute the limits: upper = 2³/3 = 8/3 and lower = 0³/3 = 0/3.
Step 4: Subtract: 8/3 − 0/3 = 8/3 = 8/3.
Answer: 8/3 square units
Common mistake: Writing 2² − 0² = 4 (skipping the integration), or integrating to 2x instead of x³/3.
Similar example: Area under y = x² from x = 0 to x = 3 is 27/3 = 9 square units.
Tip: Raise the power by 1, divide by the new power, then use upper − lower.

questions.text: The diagram shows part of the curve y = x². Find the area of the shaded region between x = 1 and x = 3.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The area under y = x² between two x-values is found by integrating: ∫x² dx = x³/3.
Step 1: From the diagram, the shaded region lies under y = x² between x = 1 and x = 3.
Step 2: Integrate: ∫ x² dx = x³/3.
Step 3: Substitute the limits: upper = 3³/3 = 27/3 and lower = 1³/3 = 1/3.
Step 4: Subtract: 27/3 − 1/3 = 26/3 = 26/3.
Answer: 26/3 square units
Common mistake: Writing 3² − 1² = 8 (skipping the integration), or integrating to 2x instead of x³/3.
Similar example: Area under y = x² from x = 0 to x = 3 is 27/3 = 9 square units.
Tip: Raise the power by 1, divide by the new power, then use upper − lower.

questions.text: The sector shown has radius 7 cm and angle 180°. Find its area. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
Concept: A sector is a slice of a circle. Its area is the fraction θ/360 of the whole circle's area, so Area = (θ/360) × πr².
Step 1: Write the fraction of the circle: 180/360 = 1/2.
Step 2: Find the area of the whole circle: πr² = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 154 cm².
Step 3: Multiply the fraction by the full area: 1/2 × 154 = 77 cm².
Answer: 77 cm².
Common mistake: 154 cm² is the area of the whole circle. A sector is only part of it.
Similar example: A sector with radius 14 cm and angle 90°: (90/360) × (22/7) × 14 × 14 = (1/4) × 616 = 154 cm².
Tip: Always simplify θ/360 first, and cancel the 7 in 22/7 against the radius to keep the numbers small.

questions.text: The bearing of Y from X is 070°. Find the bearing of X from Y.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A back bearing is the bearing of the return journey. The two bearings always differ by 180°, because the two directions are opposite.
Step 1: Look at the given bearing: 070°. It is less than 180°.
Step 2: Rule: if the bearing is less than 180°, add 180°. If it is more than 180°, subtract 180°. So we add 180°.
Step 3: 70 + 180 = 250°.
Answer: 250°.
Similar example: The bearing of B from A is 120°, so the bearing of A from B is 120 + 180 = 300°.
Tip: Bearings are written with three figures and measured clockwise from North. Write 070°, not 70°.

questions.text: The triangle PQR shown is right-angled at Q, with PQ = 6 cm and QR = 8 cm. Find PR.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Pythagoras' theorem: in a right-angled triangle, (hypotenuse)² = (side)² + (other side)². The hypotenuse is the longest side, opposite the right angle.
Step 1: The right angle is at Q, so the hypotenuse is PR (opposite Q).
Step 2: PR² = PQ² + QR² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100.
Step 3: Take the square root: PR = √100 = 10 cm.
Answer: 10 cm.
Similar example: A right triangle has sides 8 cm and 15 cm. Hypotenuse² = 64 + 225 = 289, so the hypotenuse = 17 cm.
Tip: Learn the triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25 and their multiples. They save time in the exam.

questions.text: Find the sum of the first 10 terms of the arithmetic progression 6, 11, 16, ...
questions.explanation:
Concept: An arithmetic progression (AP) goes up or down by the same amount each time, called the common difference d. The sum of the first n terms is Sₙ = n/2 × [2a + (n − 1)d], where a is the first term.
Step 1: Find a and d: a = 6, d = 11 − 6 = 5. Number of terms n = 10.
Step 2: Substitute: S = 10/2 × [2(6) + (10 − 1)(5)].
Step 3: Inside the bracket: 2(6) = 12, and (9)(5) = 45, so the bracket = 12 + 45 = 57.
Step 4: S = 10/2 × 57 = 285.
Answer: 285.
Similar example: Sum of the first 5 terms of 3, 7, 11, ...: S = 5/2 × [6 + 4(4)] = 5/2 × 22 = 55.
Tip: d is the second term minus the first. The bracket uses (n − 1), not n.

questions.text: In the isosceles triangle shown, AB = AC and each base angle is 35°. Find the angle at the vertex A.
questions.explanation:
Concept: In an isosceles triangle, the two sides AB and AC are equal, so the angles opposite them (the base angles at B and C) are equal. The three angles of any triangle add up to 180°.
Step 1: Base angles: B = C = 35°.
Step 2: Add them: 35° + 35° = 70°.
Step 3: Angle at A = 180° − 70° = 110°.
Answer: 110°.
Similar example: Base angles of 50° each: A = 180 − 100 = 80°.
Tip: Do not stop at 2 × base angle. Subtract from 180° to get the vertex angle.

questions.text: A machine bought for ₦1,500,000 depreciates at 25% per annum. Find its value after 2 years.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Depreciation means the value falls each year. Because it falls by a percentage of the new value each time, V = P(1 − r/100)ⁿ.
Step 1: P = ₦1,500,000, r = 25%, n = 2 years.
Step 2: Decay factor: 1 − 25/100 = 0.75.
Step 3: V = 1,500,000 × 0.75² = 1,500,000 × 0.5625.
Step 4: V = ₦843,750.
Answer: ₦843,750.
Similar example: A car worth ₦2,000,000 loses 10% yearly. After 2 years: 2,000,000 × 0.9² = ₦1,620,000.
Tip: Depreciation uses (1 − r/100). If you use (1 + r/100) by mistake you get the wrong, larger value.

questions.text: y varies inversely as x. If y = 12 when x = 2, find y when x = 12.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Inverse variation: y = k/x, so the product xy stays constant. First find k, then use it.
Step 1: Write the relation: y = k/x.
Step 2: Find k using y = 12, x = 2: k = xy = 2 × 12 = 24.
Step 3: The law is y = 24/x.
Step 4: When x = 12: y = 24/12 = 2.
Answer: 2.
Similar example: y varies inversely as x; y = 6 when x = 4. k = 24, so when x = 8, y = 3.
Tip: For inverse variation, check: x increases so y must decrease.

questions.text: Find the LCM of 3, 5 and 10.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The LCM (lowest common multiple) is the smallest number that every given number divides into exactly. Use prime factors: take each prime at its highest power.
Step 1: Write each number as a product of primes: 3 = 3; 5 = 5; 10 = 2 × 5.
Step 2: Take the highest power of each prime that appears: 2 × 3 × 5.
Step 3: Multiply: 2 × 3 × 5 = 30.
Step 4: Check: 30 ÷ 3 = 10, 30 ÷ 5 = 6, 30 ÷ 10 = 3. All are whole numbers.
Answer: 30.
Similar example: LCM of 4, 6 and 10: 4 = 2², 6 = 2 × 3, 10 = 2 × 5, so LCM = 2² × 3 × 5 = 60.
Tip: LCM must be at least as big as the largest number. Do not just multiply all the numbers, that gives a common multiple but not the lowest.

questions.text: In a class of 48 students, 21 offer Physics, 30 offer Chemistry and 10 offer both. How many offer neither subject?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use the Venn-diagram formula: n(P ∪ C) = n(P) + n(C) − n(P ∩ C). We subtract the overlap because students offering both were counted twice.
Step 1: Students offering at least one subject = 21 + 30 − 10 = 41.
Step 2: Total in the class = 48.
Step 3: Students offering neither = 48 − 41 = 7.
Answer: 7.
Similar example: In a class of 30, 12 offer Maths, 15 offer English and 5 offer both. Either = 12 + 15 − 5 = 22, so neither = 8.
Tip: Never forget to subtract the 'both' group once.

questions.text: Three friends share ₦48,000 in the ratio 3:4:5. What is the largest share?
questions.explanation:
Concept: To share an amount in a ratio, add the ratio numbers to get the total number of parts, find the value of one part, then multiply.
Step 1: Total parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12.
Step 2: One part = ₦48,000 ÷ 12 = ₦4,000.
Step 3: The largest ratio number is 5, so the largest share = 5 × ₦4,000 = ₦20,000.
Step 4: Check: the three shares are ₦12,000, ₦16,000 and ₦20,000. They add up to ₦48,000.
Answer: ₦20,000.
Similar example: Share ₦30,000 in the ratio 1:2:3: 6 parts, one part = ₦5,000, largest = 3 × 5,000 = ₦15,000.
Tip: Always check that your shares add up to the original amount.

questions.text: Simplify 3/4 + 1/3 − 2/3.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To add or subtract fractions, they must have the same denominator. Change every term to equivalent fractions with the LCM of the denominators.
Step 1: Find the LCM of the denominators 4, 3, 3: LCM = 12.
Step 2: Convert each term: 3/4 = 9/12; 1/3 = 4/12; 2/3 = 8/12.
Step 3: Combine the numerators and keep the denominator: (9 + 4 − 8)/12 = 5/12.
Answer: 5/12.
Similar example: 1/2 + 1/3 − 1/6: LCM = 6, so 3/6 + 2/6 − 1/6 = 4/6 = 2/3.
Tip: Never add or subtract the denominators. A whole number such as 2 is just 2/1.

questions.text: Solve for x: 7x + 8 = x + 20.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To solve a linear equation, collect the x terms on one side and the plain numbers on the other. Whatever you do to one side, do to the other.
Step 1: Start with: 7x + 8 = x + 20.
Step 2: Move the x term from the right to the left (subtract x from both sides) and the number from the left to the right: 7x − 1x = 20 − (8).
Step 3: Simplify: 6x = 12.
Step 4: Divide both sides by 6: x = 12/6 = 2.
Step 5: Check: left side = 7(2) + (8) = 22; right side = 1(2) + (20) = 22. They agree.
Answer: x = 2.
Similar example: Solve 5x − 3 = 2x + 9: 5x − 2x = 9 + 3, so 3x = 12 and x = 4.
Tip: When a term crosses the equals sign, its sign changes.

questions.text: Evaluate (3³ × 3⁴) ÷ 3³.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Laws of indices: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ and aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ. The base stays the same; only the powers are added or subtracted.
Step 1: Multiply the bracket: 3³ × 3⁴ = 3^(3+4) = 3⁷.
Step 2: Divide: 3⁷ ÷ 3³ = 3^(7−3) = 3⁴.
Step 3: Evaluate: 3⁴ = 81.
Answer: 81.
Similar example: (2³ × 2⁴) ÷ 2⁵ = 2⁷ ÷ 2⁵ = 2² = 4.
Tip: Never multiply the bases. 3³ × 3⁴ is NOT 9⁷.

questions.text: Find the remainder when x³ − 2x² + x + 1 is divided by (x − 1).
questions.explanation:
Concept: Remainder theorem: when a polynomial f(x) is divided by (x − a), the remainder is f(a). You do not need long division.
Step 1: Here f(x) = x³ − 2x² + x + 1 and the divisor is (x − 1), so a = 1.
Step 2: Substitute x = 1: f(1) = 1(1)³ − 2(1)² + 1(1) + 1.
Step 3: Evaluate each term: 1, -2, 1, 1.
Step 4: Add them: 1 − 2 + 1 + 1 = 1.
Answer: 1.
Similar example: Remainder of x² + 3x + 1 divided by (x − 2): f(2) = 4 + 6 + 1 = 11.
Tip: For (x + 3), use a = −3. The sign inside the bracket flips.

questions.text: Find the solution set of 3x − 5 > -17.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Solve an inequality like an equation. The inequality sign only reverses when you multiply or divide by a negative number.
Step 1: Start: 3x − 5 > -17.
Step 2: Move −5 to the other side (change the sign): 3x > -17 + 5 = -12.
Step 3: Divide both sides by 3 (positive, so the sign stays): x > -4.
Answer: x > -4.
Similar example: Solve 2x + 4 > 10: 2x > 6, so x > 3.
Tip: Reverse the sign only when dividing by a negative.

questions.text: Find the volume of a cone with base radius 9 cm and height 14 cm. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Volume of a cone = ⅓πr²h, which is one third of the cylinder with the same base and height.
Step 1: Write the values: r = 9 cm, h = 14 cm, π = 22/7.
Step 2: r² = 9² = 81.
Step 3: V = ⅓ × (22/7) × 81 × 14. Cancel 3 and 7 where you can.
Step 4: V = 1188 cm³.
Answer: 1188 cm³.
Similar example: Cone with r = 7 cm, h = 6 cm: ⅓ × (22/7) × 49 × 6 = 308 cm³.
Tip: A cone is ⅓ of a cylinder. Forgetting the ⅓ gives 3564 cm³, which is a common wrong option.

questions.text: A number is increased by 25% to give 100. Find the number.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A percentage increase means the new value is (100 + p)% of the original. So the original is found by dividing the new value by (1 + p/100).
Step 1: Let the original number be N. Increasing by 25% gives 125% of N.
Step 2: So N × 125/100 = 100.
Step 3: N = 100 × 100/125 = 80.
Step 4: Check: 80 × 125/100 = 100. Correct.
Answer: 80.
Similar example: A number increased by 10% gives 220. N = 220 × 100/110 = 200.
Tip: Common mistake: taking 25% of 100 and subtracting. The 25% is of the original number, not of the new one.

questions.text: Evaluate 2x² − 1x + 8 when x = 3.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To evaluate an expression, replace x with the given number. Put the number in brackets so negative signs are handled correctly, and follow BODMAS: powers first.
Step 1: Expression: 2x² − x + 8, x = 3.
Step 2: Substitute: 2(3)² − 1(3) + 8.
Step 3: Work out each term: 18, -3, 8.
Step 4: Add: 18 − 3 + 8 = 23.
Answer: 23.
Similar example: Evaluate 3x² + x − 2 at x = 2: 12 + 2 − 2 = 12.
Tip: A negative number squared is positive: (−2)² = 4, but −2² would be −4. Always use brackets.

questions.text: Find the compound interest on ₦25,000 for 2 years at 20% per annum, compounded annually.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Compound interest: each year's interest is added to the money, so the next year's interest is earned on the larger amount. A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ and Interest = A − P.
Step 1: P = ₦25,000, r = 20%, n = 2 years.
Step 2: Growth factor: 1 + 20/100 = 1.2.
Step 3: A = 25,000 × 1.2² = 25,000 × 1.44 = ₦36,000.
Step 4: Compound interest = A − P = ₦36,000 − ₦25,000 = ₦11,000.
Answer: ₦11,000.
Similar example: ₦10,000 for 2 years at 10%: A = 10,000 × 1.21 = ₦12,100, so interest = ₦2,100.
Tip: The question asks for the interest, not the final amount A. Remember to subtract P.

questions.text: Convert 64 in base ten to a number in base five.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To change a base ten number to base 5, divide repeatedly by 5 and keep the remainders. The answer is the remainders read from the bottom up.
Step 1: 64 ÷ 5 = 12 remainder 4
Step 2: 12 ÷ 5 = 2 remainder 2
Step 3: 2 ÷ 5 = 0 remainder 2
Step 4: Read the remainders from bottom to top: 224.
Answer: 224₅.
Similar example: Convert 30 to base 2: 30 → 15 r0, 7 r1, 3 r1, 1 r1, 0 r1. Read upwards: 11110₂.
Tip: Check by converting back: expand each digit of 224 by powers of 5 and add.

questions.text: If f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x² + 4, find f(g(2)).
questions.explanation:
Concept: f(g(x)) means: do g first, then put the result into f. Work from the inside bracket outwards.
Step 1: Find g(2): g(x) = x² + 4, so g(2) = 2² + 4 = 4 + 4 = 8.
Step 2: Now find f(8): f(x) = 2x + 1, so f(8) = 2 × 8 + 1 = 16 + 1 = 17.
Answer: 17.
Similar example: f(x) = x + 2, g(x) = 3x: f(g(1)) = f(3) = 5.
Tip: Compare: g(f(x)) is a different thing. The order matters.

questions.text: Evaluate 111₂ + 1110₂.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To add numbers in base two, the easiest way is: convert both to base ten, add, then convert the sum back to base two.
Step 1: 111₂ = 7 in base ten.
Step 2: 1110₂ = 14 in base ten.
Step 3: Add: 7 + 14 = 21.
Step 4: Convert back: 21 ÷ 2 = 10 r 1, 10 ÷ 2 = 5 r 0, 5 ÷ 2 = 2 r 1, 2 ÷ 2 = 1 r 0, 1 ÷ 2 = 0 r 1. Reading the remainders upwards gives 10101₂.
Answer: 10101₂.
Similar example: Evaluate 101₂ + 11₂: 5 + 3 = 8, and 8 = 1000₂.
Tip: In base 2: 1 + 1 = 10 (write 0, carry 1). Use this to check by direct column addition.

questions.text: The bar chart shows the number of students in four groups. What is the total number of students?
questions.explanation:
Concept: A bar chart shows how many items are in each group by the height of each bar. To find the total, read each bar and add them.
Step 1: Read the height of each bar from the vertical axis: 15, 11, 8, 16.
Step 2: Add all four values: 15 + 11 + 8 + 16 = 50.
Answer: 50 students.
Similar example: Bars 5, 8, 6 and 9 give 5 + 8 + 6 + 9 = 28.
Tip: Make sure you read all four bars. Missing one gives a wrong total.

questions.text: Factorise x² + 6x + 5.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To factorise x² + bx + c, find two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is b. Then x² + bx + c = (x + p)(x + r).
Step 1: We need two numbers with product 5 and sum 6.
Step 2: Factor pairs of 5: 1 × 5 (sum 6).
Step 3: The pair 5 and 1 adds to 6.
Step 4: So x² + 6x + 5 = (x + 1)(x + 5).
Answer: (x + 1)(x + 5).
Similar example: Factorise x² + 7x + 10: product 10 and sum 7 gives 2 and 5, so (x + 2)(x + 5).
Tip: Expand your answer to check: (x + p)(x + r) = x² + (p + r)x + pr.

questions.text: Find the equation of the line through (3, 2) with gradient 3.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The equation of a line through (x₁, y₁) with gradient m is y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
Step 1: Point: (3, 2), gradient m = 3.
Step 2: Substitute: y − 2 = 3(x − 3).
Step 3: Expand: y − 2 = 3x − 9.
Step 4: Add 2 to both sides: y = 3x − 9 + 2 = 3x − 7.
Answer: y = 3x − 7.
Similar example: Line through (1, 4) with gradient 2: y − 4 = 2(x − 1), so y = 2x + 2.
Tip: Check: put x = 3 into your answer. You should get y = 2.

questions.text: If f(x) = 3x + 8, find f⁻¹(29).
questions.explanation:
Concept: The inverse function f⁻¹ undoes f. To find it, write y = f(x), make x the subject, then replace y with the given number.
Step 1: Let y = 3x + 8.
Step 2: Subtract 8: y − 8 = 3x.
Step 3: Divide by 3: x = (y − 8)/3, so f⁻¹(x) = (x − 8)/3.
Step 4: f⁻¹(29) = (29 − 8)/3 = 21/3 = 7.
Answer: 7.
Similar example: f(x) = 2x + 3: f⁻¹(x) = (x − 3)/2, so f⁻¹(11) = 4.
Tip: Shortcut: f⁻¹(29) is the x that gives f(x) = 29. Solve the equation directly.

questions.text: Find the area of the trapezium shown.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. Its area = ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × (perpendicular height).
Step 1: Read from the diagram: parallel sides 5 cm and 14 cm, perpendicular height 8 cm.
Step 2: Add the parallel sides: 5 + 14 = 19.
Step 3: Area = ½ × 19 × 8 = 76 cm².
Answer: 76 cm².
Similar example: Parallel sides 6 and 10, height 4: ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 cm².
Tip: Use the perpendicular height, not the slanting side.

questions.text: Convert 100011₂ to a number in base ten.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Each digit in a base 2 number has a place value that is a power of 2, starting from 2⁰ = 1 on the right. Multiply each digit by its place value and add.
Step 1: Write the place values from right to left: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32.
Step 2: Expand: 100011₂ = 1 × 2⁵ + 0 × 2⁴ + 0 × 2³ + 0 × 2² + 1 × 2 + 1 × 1.
Step 3: Work out each term: 32 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 35.
Answer: 35.
Similar example: Convert 101₂: 1 × 4 + 0 × 2 + 1 × 1 = 5.
Tip: Number the place values from the right, starting at power 0.

questions.text: If U = {1, 2, 3, ..., 12} and A = {multiples of 4 in U}, find A′.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The complement A′ is the set of all elements of the universal set U that are NOT in A.
Step 1: List U = {1, 2, 3, ..., 12}.
Step 2: List A, the multiples of 4 in U: A = {4, 8, 12}.
Step 3: Remove these from U: A′ = {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11}.
Answer: A′ = {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11}.
Similar example: U = {1, ..., 8}, A = {multiples of 4} = {4, 8}, so A′ = {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7}.
Tip: Count: n(A) + n(A′) must equal n(U). Here 3 + 9 = 12.

questions.text: A binary operation * is defined by a * b = a² + 2b − ab. Evaluate 4 * 2.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A binary operation is a rule that combines two numbers a and b. To evaluate it, replace a and b by the given numbers and follow BODMAS.
Step 1: The rule: a * b = a² + 2b − ab.
Step 2: Here a = 4 and b = 2.
Step 3: Substitute: 4² + 2(2) − 4(2) = 16 + 4 − 8.
Step 4: = 12.
Answer: 12.
Similar example: If a * b = a² − b + ab, then 2 * 3 = 4 − 3 + 6 = 7.
Tip: Use a as the first number and b as the second. 4 * 2 is not the same as 2 * 4.

questions.text: In the right-angled triangle ABC shown, find cos θ.
questions.explanation:
Concept: SOH-CAH-TOA: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite/adjacent. 'Opposite' faces angle θ, 'adjacent' touches θ, and the hypotenuse faces the right angle.
Step 1: From the diagram, the sides are: opposite = 3, adjacent = 4, hypotenuse = 5. (Check: 3² + 4² = 25 = 5².)
Step 2: Write the rule: cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse.
Step 3: Substitute: cos θ = 4/5.
Answer: 4/5.
Similar example: Sides 3, 4, 5 with opposite = 3: sin θ = 3/5, cos θ = 4/5, tan θ = 3/4.
Tip: Label the sides from the angle θ first, then pick the correct ratio. The hypotenuse is always the longest side.

questions.text: Find the gradient of the curve y = 3x³ − 1x at x = 2.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The gradient of a curve at a point is the value of the derivative dy/dx at that point. First differentiate, then substitute the x-value.
Step 1: Differentiate: y = 3x³ − x, so dy/dx = 9x² − 1.
Step 2: Substitute x = 2: 9(2)² − 1.
Step 3: Evaluate: 36 − 1 = 35.
Answer: 35.
Similar example: Gradient of y = x³ + 2x at x = 1: dy/dx = 3x² + 2 = 5.
Tip: Differentiate first, substitute after. Never substitute into y first.

questions.text: The pie chart shown represents 180 students. How many students are represented by the 130° sector?
questions.explanation:
Concept: In a pie chart, the whole circle (360°) stands for all the students. A sector of angle θ stands for θ/360 of the total.
Step 1: Fraction for the sector = 130/360 = 13/36.
Step 2: Number of students = 13/36 × 180.
Step 3: = 65.
Answer: 65 students.
Similar example: A 60° sector in a pie chart for 120 students: (60/360) × 120 = 20.
Tip: Check: all the sector angles must add up to 360°.

questions.text: Find the median of 22, 2, 7, 18, 3, 5, 15.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The median is the middle value when the data is arranged in order. With an odd number of values, it is the value at position (n + 1)/2.
Step 1: Arrange in ascending order: 2, 3, 5, 7, 15, 18, 22.
Step 2: There are 7 values, so the median is the 4th value.
Step 3: The 4th value is 7.
Answer: 7.
Similar example: Median of 9, 2, 5, 7, 4: ordered 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, so the median is 5.
Tip: You must arrange the numbers first. The middle value of the unordered list is wrong.

questions.text: A trader bought an article for ₦2,500 and sold it for ₦3,250. Find the percentage profit.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Profit = selling price − cost price. Percentage profit = (profit ÷ cost price) × 100%.
Step 1: Profit = ₦3,250 − ₦2,500 = ₦750.
Step 2: Divide by the cost price: 750/2500.
Step 3: Percentage profit = 750/2500 × 100 = 30%.
Answer: 30%.
Similar example: Bought for ₦500, sold for ₦600: profit 100, so (100/500) × 100 = 20%.
Tip: Percentage profit is always based on the cost price, not the selling price.

questions.text: Evaluate ∫ (6x² + 2x) dx from x = 0 to x = 1.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To integrate a power of x: ∫axⁿ dx = a xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1). For a definite integral, substitute the upper limit, then subtract the value at the lower limit.
Step 1: Integrate term by term: ∫(6x² + 2x) dx = 2x³ + 1x².
Step 2: Substitute x = 1: 2(1)³ + 1(1)² = 3.
Step 3: Substitute x = 0: the value is 0.
Step 4: Subtract: 3 − 0 = 3.
Answer: 3.
Similar example: ∫(4x + 3x²) dx from 0 to 2 = [2x² + x³] = 8 + 8 = 16.
Tip: Add 1 to the power and divide by the new power. No '+ C' is needed for definite integrals.

questions.text: Find the simple interest on ₦5,000 for 2 years at 6% per annum.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Simple interest is earned only on the original sum. I = (P × R × T)/100, where P is the principal, R is the yearly rate (%), and T is the time in years.
Step 1: P = ₦5,000, R = 6%, T = 2 years.
Step 2: I = (5,000 × 6 × 2)/100.
Step 3: 5,000 ÷ 100 = 50, then 50 × 6 × 2 = ₦600.
Answer: ₦600.
Similar example: ₦8,000 for 3 years at 5%: 8000/100 × 5 × 3 = ₦1,200.
Tip: Divide by 100 first to keep the arithmetic small.

questions.text: A car covers 100 km in 1 hour 15 minutes. Find its average speed in km/h.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time, with the time in hours.
Step 1: Convert the time to hours: 1 h 15 min = 1 + 15/60 = 5/4 hours.
Step 2: Speed = 100 ÷ 5/4.
Step 3: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: 100 × 4/5 = 80 km/h.
Answer: 80 km/h.
Similar example: 150 km in 2 h 30 min: time = 5/2 h, speed = 150 × 2/5 = 60 km/h.
Tip: Never write 1 h 15 min as 1.15. Use 1 + 15/60 = 1.25.

questions.text: From a point P on level ground 20 m from the foot B of a tower TB, the angle of elevation of the top T is 60°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The angle of elevation is the angle above the horizontal. In the right triangle TBP, tan(angle) = opposite/adjacent = TB/PB.
Step 1: Identify: adjacent side PB = 20 m (on the ground), opposite side TB = height.
Step 2: Write: tan 60° = TB/20, so TB = 20 × tan 60°.
Step 3: Use the exact value: tan 60° = √3.
Step 4: TB = 20 × √3 = 20√3 m.
Answer: 20√3 m.
Similar example: Distance 12 m, elevation 60°: height = 12 × √3 = 12√3 m.
Tip: Memorise: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

questions.text: Find the minimum value of y = x² − 4x + 17.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the square: x² − bx + c = (x − b/2)² + (c − b²/4). A square is never negative, so the smallest value occurs when (x − b/2)² = 0.
Step 1: Half of the x-coefficient: 4/2 = 2.
Step 2: x² − 4x = (x − 2)² − 4.
Step 3: So y = (x − 2)² − 4 + 17 = (x − 2)² + 13.
Step 4: The smallest value of (x − 2)² is 0 (at x = 2), so the minimum value of y = 13.
Answer: 13.
Similar example: Minimum of y = x² − 6x + 10 = (x − 3)² + 1, which is 1.
Tip: Calculus check: dy/dx = 2x − 4 = 0 gives x = 2, the same turning point.

questions.text: Solve for x: 4x − 6 = x + 21.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To solve a linear equation, collect the x terms on one side and the plain numbers on the other. Whatever you do to one side, do to the other.
Step 1: Start with: 4x − 6 = x + 21.
Step 2: Move the x term from the right to the left (subtract x from both sides) and the number from the left to the right: 4x − 1x = 21 − (-6).
Step 3: Simplify: 3x = 27.
Step 4: Divide both sides by 3: x = 27/3 = 9.
Step 5: Check: left side = 4(9) + (-6) = 30; right side = 1(9) + (21) = 30. They agree.
Answer: x = 9.
Similar example: Solve 5x − 3 = 2x + 9: 5x − 2x = 9 + 3, so 3x = 12 and x = 4.
Tip: When a term crosses the equals sign, its sign changes.

questions.text: From a point P on level ground 30 m from the foot B of a tower TB, the angle of elevation of the top T is 45°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The angle of elevation is the angle above the horizontal. In the right triangle TBP, tan(angle) = opposite/adjacent = TB/PB.
Step 1: Identify: adjacent side PB = 30 m (on the ground), opposite side TB = height.
Step 2: Write: tan 45° = TB/30, so TB = 30 × tan 45°.
Step 3: Use the exact value: tan 45° = 1.
Step 4: TB = 30 × 1 = 30 m.
Answer: 30 m.
Similar example: Distance 12 m, elevation 60°: height = 12 × √3 = 12√3 m.
Tip: Memorise: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

questions.text: If f(x) = 5x + 1, find f⁻¹(11).
questions.explanation:
Concept: The inverse function f⁻¹ undoes f. To find it, write y = f(x), make x the subject, then replace y with the given number.
Step 1: Let y = 5x + 1.
Step 2: Subtract 1: y − 1 = 5x.
Step 3: Divide by 5: x = (y − 1)/5, so f⁻¹(x) = (x − 1)/5.
Step 4: f⁻¹(11) = (11 − 1)/5 = 10/5 = 2.
Answer: 2.
Similar example: f(x) = 2x + 3: f⁻¹(x) = (x − 3)/2, so f⁻¹(11) = 4.
Tip: Shortcut: f⁻¹(29) is the x that gives f(x) = 29. Solve the equation directly.

questions.text: The triangle PQR shown is right-angled at Q, with PR = 13 cm and PQ = 5 cm. Find QR.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Pythagoras' theorem: (hypotenuse)² = (side)² + (other side)². When the hypotenuse is given, subtract to find a shorter side.
Step 1: PR is opposite the right angle at Q, so PR = 13 cm is the hypotenuse.
Step 2: Rearrange: QR² = PR² − PQ² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144.
Step 3: Take the square root: QR = √144 = 12 cm.
Answer: 12 cm.
Common mistake: adding the squares (13² + 5² ) gives the wrong answer when the hypotenuse is already given.
Similar example: Hypotenuse 10 cm, one side 6 cm: other side² = 100 − 36 = 64, so the side = 8 cm.
Tip: Hypotenuse given means subtract. Two short sides given means add.

questions.text: The 2nd term of a GP is 2 and the 5th term is 16. Find the common ratio.
questions.explanation:
Concept: In a GP, each term is the previous term × r. So the jth term = the ith term × r^(j − i). Divide the later term by the earlier term to isolate a power of r.
Step 1: Write the terms: T2 = ar^1 = 2 and T5 = ar^4 = 16.
Step 2: Divide: T5/T2 = r^3, so r^3 = 16/2 = 8.
Step 3: Take the cube root: r = ∛8 = 2.
Step 4: Check: 2 × 2^3 = 16, which equals 16.
Answer: 2.
Similar example: T2 = 3 and T4 = 12: r² = 4, so r = 2.
Tip: The number of steps between the terms (j − i) is the power of r.

questions.text: Factorise x² + 6x + 8.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To factorise x² + bx + c, find two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is b. Then x² + bx + c = (x + p)(x + r).
Step 1: We need two numbers with product 8 and sum 6.
Step 2: Factor pairs of 8: 1 × 8 (sum 9), 2 × 4 (sum 6).
Step 3: The pair 4 and 2 adds to 6.
Step 4: So x² + 6x + 8 = (x + 2)(x + 4).
Answer: (x + 2)(x + 4).
Similar example: Factorise x² + 7x + 10: product 10 and sum 7 gives 2 and 5, so (x + 2)(x + 5).
Tip: Expand your answer to check: (x + p)(x + r) = x² + (p + r)x + pr.

questions.text: Find the compound interest on ₦5,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Compound interest: each year's interest is added to the money, so the next year's interest is earned on the larger amount. A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ and Interest = A − P.
Step 1: P = ₦5,000, r = 10%, n = 2 years.
Step 2: Growth factor: 1 + 10/100 = 1.1.
Step 3: A = 5,000 × 1.1² = 5,000 × 1.21 = ₦6,050.
Step 4: Compound interest = A − P = ₦6,050 − ₦5,000 = ₦1,050.
Answer: ₦1,050.
Similar example: ₦10,000 for 2 years at 10%: A = 10,000 × 1.21 = ₦12,100, so interest = ₦2,100.
Tip: The question asks for the interest, not the final amount A. Remember to subtract P.

questions.text: Convert 131 in base ten to a number in base eight.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To change a base ten number to base 8, divide repeatedly by 8 and keep the remainders. The answer is the remainders read from the bottom up.
Step 1: 131 ÷ 8 = 16 remainder 3
Step 2: 16 ÷ 8 = 2 remainder 0
Step 3: 2 ÷ 8 = 0 remainder 2
Step 4: Read the remainders from bottom to top: 203.
Answer: 203₈.
Similar example: Convert 30 to base 2: 30 → 15 r0, 7 r1, 3 r1, 1 r1, 0 r1. Read upwards: 11110₂.
Tip: Check by converting back: expand each digit of 203 by powers of 8 and add.

questions.text: The bar chart shows the number of students in four groups. How many more students are in the largest group than in the smallest group?
questions.explanation:
Concept: To compare bars, read the tallest and shortest bars from the vertical axis, then subtract: difference = largest − smallest.
Step 1: The tallest bar is 15 and the shortest bar is 8.
Step 2: Difference = 15 − 8 = 7.
Answer: 7 students.
Similar example: Tallest 20, shortest 12: 20 − 12 = 8 more students.
Tip: Subtract the smallest from the largest, not the other way.

questions.text: Find the value of x for which the matrix [x 2; 6 3] is singular.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A matrix is singular when its determinant is zero. For [a b; c d], the determinant = ad − bc.
Step 1: The matrix is [x 2; 6 3]. Determinant = x × 3 − 2 × 6 = 3x − 12.
Step 2: Set the determinant to zero: 3x − 12 = 0.
Step 3: 3x = 12, so x = 12/3 = 4.
Answer: x = 4.
Similar example: Matrix [x 4; 3 6] is singular when 6x − 12 = 0, so x = 2.
Tip: Singular means no inverse, which happens when the determinant is 0.

questions.text: Find the LCM of 6, 9 and 12.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The LCM (lowest common multiple) is the smallest number that every given number divides into exactly. Use prime factors: take each prime at its highest power.
Step 1: Write each number as a product of primes: 6 = 2 × 3; 9 = 3²; 12 = 2² × 3.
Step 2: Take the highest power of each prime that appears: 2² × 3².
Step 3: Multiply: 2² × 3² = 36.
Step 4: Check: 36 ÷ 6 = 6, 36 ÷ 9 = 4, 36 ÷ 12 = 3. All are whole numbers.
Answer: 36.
Similar example: LCM of 4, 6 and 10: 4 = 2², 6 = 2 × 3, 10 = 2 × 5, so LCM = 2² × 3 × 5 = 60.
Tip: LCM must be at least as big as the largest number. Do not just multiply all the numbers, that gives a common multiple but not the lowest.

questions.text: Differentiate y = 5x⁴ − 4x² + 8 with respect to x.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To differentiate a power of x: dy/dx of axⁿ = n × a × xⁿ⁻¹. Multiply by the power, then reduce the power by 1. A constant differentiates to 0.
Step 1: Differentiate term by term: 5x⁴ → 5 × 4 = 20, power 4−1 = 3: 20x³; −4x² → −4 × 2 = −8, power 2−1 = 1: −8x; 8 (a constant) → 0.
Step 2: Combine: dy/dx = 20x³ − 8x.
Answer: dy/dx = 20x³ − 8x.
Similar example: y = 3x⁴ − 5x + 2: dy/dx = 12x³ − 5.
Tip: Check that the constant term disappears and each power drops by exactly 1.

questions.text: The bearing of Y from X is 220°. Find the bearing of X from Y.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A back bearing is the bearing of the return journey. The two bearings always differ by 180°, because the two directions are opposite.
Step 1: Look at the given bearing: 220°. It is more than 180°.
Step 2: Rule: if the bearing is less than 180°, add 180°. If it is more than 180°, subtract 180°. So we subtract 180°.
Step 3: 220 − 180 = 40°.
Answer: 040°.
Similar example: The bearing of B from A is 120°, so the bearing of A from B is 120 + 180 = 300°.
Tip: Bearings are written with three figures and measured clockwise from North. Write 070°, not 70°.

questions.text: Find the 13th term of the arithmetic progression 6, 8, 10, ...
questions.explanation:
Concept: In an AP, the nth term is Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d, where a is the first term and d is the common difference.
Step 1: Find a and d: a = 6, d = 8 − 6 = 2.
Step 2: The term wanted is n = 13, so n − 1 = 12.
Step 3: Substitute: T = 6 + (12)(2) = 6 + 24.
Step 4: T = 30.
Answer: 30.
Similar example: 10th term of 5, 8, 11, ...: 5 + 9(3) = 32.
Tip: The 12th term needs 11 jumps of d, not 12.

questions.text: An arc of a circle subtends an angle of 50° at the centre. Find the angle it subtends at the circumference.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Circle theorem: the angle an arc makes at the centre is twice the angle it makes at the circumference.
Step 1: The angle at the centre is 50°.
Step 2: Angle at circumference = (angle at centre) ÷ 2.
Step 3: 50 ÷ 2 = 25°.
Answer: 25°.
Similar example: Angle at the centre = 120°, so the angle at the circumference = 60°.
Tip: Centre is the bigger angle; circumference is the smaller. Always halve to go from centre to circumference.

questions.text: In the right-angled triangle ABC shown, find sin θ.
questions.explanation:
Concept: SOH-CAH-TOA: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite/adjacent. 'Opposite' faces angle θ, 'adjacent' touches θ, and the hypotenuse faces the right angle.
Step 1: From the diagram, the sides are: opposite = 5, adjacent = 12, hypotenuse = 13. (Check: 5² + 12² = 169 = 13².)
Step 2: Write the rule: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse.
Step 3: Substitute: sin θ = 5/13.
Answer: 5/13.
Similar example: Sides 3, 4, 5 with opposite = 3: sin θ = 3/5, cos θ = 4/5, tan θ = 3/4.
Tip: Label the sides from the angle θ first, then pick the correct ratio. The hypotenuse is always the longest side.

questions.text: Find the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with 12 sides.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The interior angles of an n-sided polygon add up to (n − 2) × 180°. This comes from splitting the polygon into (n − 2) triangles.
Step 1: The number of sides is n = 12.
Step 2: Number of triangles = n − 2 = 12 − 2 = 10.
Step 3: Sum = 10 × 180° = 1800°.
Answer: 1800°.
Similar example: A hexagon (6 sides): (6 − 2) × 180 = 720°.
Tip: Check with a triangle: (3 − 2) × 180 = 180°. The formula works.

questions.text: A trader bought an article for ₦2,000 and sold it for ₦2,600. Find the percentage profit.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Profit = selling price − cost price. Percentage profit = (profit ÷ cost price) × 100%.
Step 1: Profit = ₦2,600 − ₦2,000 = ₦600.
Step 2: Divide by the cost price: 600/2000.
Step 3: Percentage profit = 600/2000 × 100 = 30%.
Answer: 30%.
Similar example: Bought for ₦500, sold for ₦600: profit 100, so (100/500) × 100 = 20%.
Tip: Percentage profit is always based on the cost price, not the selling price.

questions.text: Evaluate 11011₂ + 11011₂.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To add numbers in base two, the easiest way is: convert both to base ten, add, then convert the sum back to base two.
Step 1: 11011₂ = 27 in base ten.
Step 2: 11011₂ = 27 in base ten.
Step 3: Add: 27 + 27 = 54.
Step 4: Convert back: 54 ÷ 2 = 27 r 0, 27 ÷ 2 = 13 r 1, 13 ÷ 2 = 6 r 1, 6 ÷ 2 = 3 r 0, 3 ÷ 2 = 1 r 1, 1 ÷ 2 = 0 r 1. Reading the remainders upwards gives 110110₂.
Answer: 110110₂.
Similar example: Evaluate 101₂ + 11₂: 5 + 3 = 8, and 8 = 1000₂.
Tip: In base 2: 1 + 1 = 10 (write 0, carry 1). Use this to check by direct column addition.

questions.text: The sum of two numbers is 41 and their difference is 21. Find the larger number.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Let the larger number be x and the smaller y. Then x + y = sum and x − y = difference. Adding the two equations removes y.
Step 1: x + y = 41 and x − y = 21.
Step 2: Add: 2x = 41 + 21 = 62.
Step 3: x = 62/2 = 31.
Step 4: Smaller number y = 41 − 31 = 10. Check: difference = 31 − 10 = 21.
Answer: 31.
Similar example: Sum 30, difference 6: larger = (30 + 6)/2 = 18, smaller = 12.
Tip: Larger = (sum + difference)/2 and smaller = (sum − difference)/2.

questions.text: Find the gradient of the curve y = 3x³ − 4x at x = 3.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The gradient of a curve at a point is the value of the derivative dy/dx at that point. First differentiate, then substitute the x-value.
Step 1: Differentiate: y = 3x³ − 4x, so dy/dx = 9x² − 4.
Step 2: Substitute x = 3: 9(3)² − 4.
Step 3: Evaluate: 81 − 4 = 77.
Answer: 77.
Similar example: Gradient of y = x³ + 2x at x = 1: dy/dx = 3x² + 2 = 5.
Tip: Differentiate first, substitute after. Never substitute into y first.

questions.text: Convert 232₅ to a number in base ten.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Each digit in a base 5 number has a place value that is a power of 5, starting from 5⁰ = 1 on the right. Multiply each digit by its place value and add.
Step 1: Write the place values from right to left: 1, 5, 25.
Step 2: Expand: 232₅ = 2 × 5² + 3 × 5 + 2 × 1.
Step 3: Work out each term: 50 + 15 + 2 = 67.
Answer: 67.
Similar example: Convert 101₂: 1 × 4 + 0 × 2 + 1 × 1 = 5.
Tip: Number the place values from the right, starting at power 0.

questions.text: A car covers 108 km in 1 hour 30 minutes. Find its average speed in km/h.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time, with the time in hours.
Step 1: Convert the time to hours: 1 h 30 min = 1 + 30/60 = 3/2 hours.
Step 2: Speed = 108 ÷ 3/2.
Step 3: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: 108 × 2/3 = 72 km/h.
Answer: 72 km/h.
Similar example: 150 km in 2 h 30 min: time = 5/2 h, speed = 150 × 2/5 = 60 km/h.
Tip: Never write 1 h 15 min as 1.15. Use 1 + 15/60 = 1.25.

questions.text: y varies inversely as x. If y = 3 when x = 4, find y when x = 6.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Inverse variation: y = k/x, so the product xy stays constant. First find k, then use it.
Step 1: Write the relation: y = k/x.
Step 2: Find k using y = 3, x = 4: k = xy = 4 × 3 = 12.
Step 3: The law is y = 12/x.
Step 4: When x = 6: y = 12/6 = 2.
Answer: 2.
Similar example: y varies inversely as x; y = 6 when x = 4. k = 24, so when x = 8, y = 3.
Tip: For inverse variation, check: x increases so y must decrease.

questions.text: Find the area of the trapezium shown.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. Its area = ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × (perpendicular height).
Step 1: Read from the diagram: parallel sides 7 cm and 15 cm, perpendicular height 3 cm.
Step 2: Add the parallel sides: 7 + 15 = 22.
Step 3: Area = ½ × 22 × 3 = 33 cm².
Answer: 33 cm².
Similar example: Parallel sides 6 and 10, height 4: ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 cm².
Tip: Use the perpendicular height, not the slanting side.

questions.text: Find the remainder when x³ − 3x² + 5 is divided by (x − 1).
questions.explanation:
Concept: Remainder theorem: when a polynomial f(x) is divided by (x − a), the remainder is f(a). You do not need long division.
Step 1: Here f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 5 and the divisor is (x − 1), so a = 1.
Step 2: Substitute x = 1: f(1) = 1(1)³ − 3(1)² + 5.
Step 3: Evaluate each term: 1, -3, 5.
Step 4: Add them: 1 − 3 + 5 = 3.
Answer: 3.
Similar example: Remainder of x² + 3x + 1 divided by (x − 2): f(2) = 4 + 6 + 1 = 11.
Tip: For (x + 3), use a = −3. The sign inside the bracket flips.

questions.text: In the isosceles triangle shown, AB = AC and each base angle is 72°. Find the angle at the vertex A.
questions.explanation:
Concept: In an isosceles triangle, the two sides AB and AC are equal, so the angles opposite them (the base angles at B and C) are equal. The three angles of any triangle add up to 180°.
Step 1: Base angles: B = C = 72°.
Step 2: Add them: 72° + 72° = 144°.
Step 3: Angle at A = 180° − 144° = 36°.
Answer: 36°.
Similar example: Base angles of 50° each: A = 180 − 100 = 80°.
Tip: Do not stop at 2 × base angle. Subtract from 180° to get the vertex angle.

questions.text: If U = {1, 2, 3, ..., 10} and A = {multiples of 3 in U}, find A′.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The complement A′ is the set of all elements of the universal set U that are NOT in A.
Step 1: List U = {1, 2, 3, ..., 10}.
Step 2: List A, the multiples of 3 in U: A = {3, 6, 9}.
Step 3: Remove these from U: A′ = {1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10}.
Answer: A′ = {1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10}.
Similar example: U = {1, ..., 8}, A = {multiples of 4} = {4, 8}, so A′ = {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7}.
Tip: Count: n(A) + n(A′) must equal n(U). Here 3 + 7 = 10.

questions.text: Find the median of 23, 4, 17, 8, 22, 14, 11.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The median is the middle value when the data is arranged in order. With an odd number of values, it is the value at position (n + 1)/2.
Step 1: Arrange in ascending order: 4, 8, 11, 14, 17, 22, 23.
Step 2: There are 7 values, so the median is the 4th value.
Step 3: The 4th value is 14.
Answer: 14.
Similar example: Median of 9, 2, 5, 7, 4: ordered 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, so the median is 5.
Tip: You must arrange the numbers first. The middle value of the unordered list is wrong.

questions.text: A number is increased by 20% to give 96. Find the number.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A percentage increase means the new value is (100 + p)% of the original. So the original is found by dividing the new value by (1 + p/100).
Step 1: Let the original number be N. Increasing by 20% gives 120% of N.
Step 2: So N × 120/100 = 96.
Step 3: N = 96 × 100/120 = 80.
Step 4: Check: 80 × 120/100 = 96. Correct.
Answer: 80.
Similar example: A number increased by 10% gives 220. N = 220 × 100/110 = 200.
Tip: Common mistake: taking 20% of 96 and subtracting. The 20% is of the original number, not of the new one.

questions.text: If f(x) = 3x + 1 and g(x) = x² + 2, find f(g(3)).
questions.explanation:
Concept: f(g(x)) means: do g first, then put the result into f. Work from the inside bracket outwards.
Step 1: Find g(3): g(x) = x² + 2, so g(3) = 3² + 2 = 9 + 2 = 11.
Step 2: Now find f(11): f(x) = 3x + 1, so f(11) = 3 × 11 + 1 = 33 + 1 = 34.
Answer: 34.
Similar example: f(x) = x + 2, g(x) = 3x: f(g(1)) = f(3) = 5.
Tip: Compare: g(f(x)) is a different thing. The order matters.

questions.text: The sector shown has radius 21 cm and angle 180°. Find its area. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
Concept: A sector is a slice of a circle. Its area is the fraction θ/360 of the whole circle's area, so Area = (θ/360) × πr².
Step 1: Write the fraction of the circle: 180/360 = 1/2.
Step 2: Find the area of the whole circle: πr² = (22/7) × 21 × 21 = 1386 cm².
Step 3: Multiply the fraction by the full area: 1/2 × 1386 = 693 cm².
Answer: 693 cm².
Common mistake: 1386 cm² is the area of the whole circle. A sector is only part of it.
Similar example: A sector with radius 14 cm and angle 90°: (90/360) × (22/7) × 14 × 14 = (1/4) × 616 = 154 cm².
Tip: Always simplify θ/360 first, and cancel the 7 in 22/7 against the radius to keep the numbers small.

questions.text: Simplify 2 + 1/4 − 1/3.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To add or subtract fractions, they must have the same denominator. Change every term to equivalent fractions with the LCM of the denominators.
Step 1: Find the LCM of the denominators 1, 4, 3: LCM = 12.
Step 2: Convert each term: 2 = 24/12; 1/4 = 3/12; 1/3 = 4/12.
Step 3: Combine the numerators and keep the denominator: (24 + 3 − 4)/12 = 23/12.
Answer: 23/12.
Similar example: 1/2 + 1/3 − 1/6: LCM = 6, so 3/6 + 2/6 − 1/6 = 4/6 = 2/3.
Tip: Never add or subtract the denominators. A whole number such as 2 is just 2/1.

questions.text: Evaluate ∫ (6x² + 4x) dx from x = 0 to x = 3.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To integrate a power of x: ∫axⁿ dx = a xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1). For a definite integral, substitute the upper limit, then subtract the value at the lower limit.
Step 1: Integrate term by term: ∫(6x² + 4x) dx = 2x³ + 2x².
Step 2: Substitute x = 3: 2(3)³ + 2(3)² = 72.
Step 3: Substitute x = 0: the value is 0.
Step 4: Subtract: 72 − 0 = 72.
Answer: 72.
Similar example: ∫(4x + 3x²) dx from 0 to 2 = [2x² + x³] = 8 + 8 = 16.
Tip: Add 1 to the power and divide by the new power. No '+ C' is needed for definite integrals.

questions.text: The pie chart shown represents 180 students. How many students are represented by the 180° sector?
questions.explanation:
Concept: In a pie chart, the whole circle (360°) stands for all the students. A sector of angle θ stands for θ/360 of the total.
Step 1: Fraction for the sector = 180/360 = 1/2.
Step 2: Number of students = 1/2 × 180.
Step 3: = 90.
Answer: 90 students.
Similar example: A 60° sector in a pie chart for 120 students: (60/360) × 120 = 20.
Tip: Check: all the sector angles must add up to 360°.

questions.text: In how many ways can a chairman and a secretary be chosen from 5 people?
questions.explanation:
Concept: When the order matters (chairman and secretary are different posts), use permutations: ⁿPᵣ = n!/(n − r)!.
Step 1: The two posts are different, so order matters: this is a permutation.
Step 2: First post: 5 choices. Second post: 4 choices (one person is already used).
Step 3: Total = 5 × 4 = 20.
Answer: 20 ways.
Similar example: Choosing a president and vice-president from 6 people: 6 × 5 = 30.
Tip: Different roles mean permutation. A team with no roles is a combination.

questions.text: If log₁₀2 = 0.3010 and log₁₀3 = 0.4771, find log₁₀(54).
questions.explanation:
Concept: Laws of logarithms: log(xy) = log x + log y, and log(xⁿ) = n log x. Write the number using only the primes 2 and 3.
Step 1: Break 54 into factors of 2 and 3: 54 = 2 × 3³.
Step 2: Use the product and power laws: log 54 = 1 × log 2 + 3 × log 3.
Step 3: Substitute: 1(0.3010) + 3(0.4771) = 0.3010 + 1.4313.
Step 4: = 1.7323.
Answer: 1.7323.
Similar example: log 12 = log (2² × 3) = 2(0.3010) + 0.4771 = 1.0791.
Tip: Use prime factorisation. It turns any such number into a sum of the two given logs.

questions.text: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides 2 cm and 3 cm. Find the ratio of their areas.
questions.explanation:
Concept: For similar shapes, if the lengths are in ratio a : b, the areas are in ratio a² : b².
Step 1: Ratio of sides = 2 : 3.
Step 2: Square both numbers: 2² : 3² = 4 : 9.
Step 3: Simplify if possible: 4 : 9.
Answer: 4:9.
Similar example: Sides 2 cm and 5 cm give an area ratio of 4 : 25.
Tip: Lengths use the ratio, areas use the ratio squared, volumes use the ratio cubed.

questions.text: A binary operation * is defined by a * b = a² + b − ab. Evaluate 5 * 5.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A binary operation is a rule that combines two numbers a and b. To evaluate it, replace a and b by the given numbers and follow BODMAS.
Step 1: The rule: a * b = a² + b − ab.
Step 2: Here a = 5 and b = 5.
Step 3: Substitute: 5² + 5 − 5(5) = 25 + 5 − 25.
Step 4: = 5.
Answer: 5.
Similar example: If a * b = a² − b + ab, then 2 * 3 = 4 − 3 + 6 = 7.
Tip: Use a as the first number and b as the second. 4 * 2 is not the same as 2 * 4.

questions.text: Solve for x: 5^(2x − 2) = 5².
questions.explanation:
Concept: If two powers have the same base and are equal, their indices must be equal: if aᵐ = aⁿ then m = n.
Step 1: Both sides have base 5, so equate the powers.
Step 2: 2x − 2 = 2.
Step 3: 2x = 2 + 2 = 4.
Step 4: x = 4/2 = 2.
Answer: x = 2.
Similar example: Solve 2^(x + 1) = 2⁵: x + 1 = 5, so x = 4.
Tip: Make the bases the same first. Then compare the indices.

questions.text: A binary operation * is defined by a * b = a² + 2b − ab. Evaluate 5 * 5.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A binary operation is a rule that combines two numbers a and b. To evaluate it, replace a and b by the given numbers and follow BODMAS.
Step 1: The rule: a * b = a² + 2b − ab.
Step 2: Here a = 5 and b = 5.
Step 3: Substitute: 5² + 2(5) − 5(5) = 25 + 10 − 25.
Step 4: = 10.
Answer: 10.
Similar example: If a * b = a² − b + ab, then 2 * 3 = 4 − 3 + 6 = 7.
Tip: Use a as the first number and b as the second. 4 * 2 is not the same as 2 * 4.

questions.text: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 9 cm. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Volume of a cylinder = πr²h (area of the circular base × height).
Step 1: Write the values: r = 7 cm, h = 9 cm, π = 22/7.
Step 2: Base area = πr² = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 154 cm².
Step 3: Multiply by the height: 154 × 9 = 1386 cm³.
Answer: 1386 cm³.
Similar example: r = 7 cm, h = 10 cm: (22/7) × 49 × 10 = 1540 cm³.
Tip: Square the radius only, not the height.

questions.text: Find the area of the trapezium shown.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. Its area = ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × (perpendicular height).
Step 1: Read from the diagram: parallel sides 4 cm and 10 cm, perpendicular height 3 cm.
Step 2: Add the parallel sides: 4 + 10 = 14.
Step 3: Area = ½ × 14 × 3 = 21 cm².
Answer: 21 cm².
Similar example: Parallel sides 6 and 10, height 4: ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 cm².
Tip: Use the perpendicular height, not the slanting side.

questions.text: Find the 4th term of the geometric progression 1, 2, 4, ...
questions.explanation:
Concept: A geometric progression (GP) multiplies by the same number each time, the common ratio r. The nth term is Tₙ = a·rⁿ⁻¹.
Step 1: First term a = 1. Common ratio r = 2 ÷ 1 = 2.
Step 2: For the 4th term, the power is n − 1 = 3.
Step 3: T = 1 × 2^3 = 1 × 8 = 8.
Step 4: Check by continuing the pattern: 1, 2, 4, 8.
Answer: 8.
Similar example: 5th term of 3, 6, 12, ...: 3 × 2⁴ = 48.
Tip: GP: multiply by r. AP: add d. Do not mix them up.

questions.text: A car covers 60 km in 1 hour 15 minutes. Find its average speed in km/h.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time, with the time in hours.
Step 1: Convert the time to hours: 1 h 15 min = 1 + 15/60 = 5/4 hours.
Step 2: Speed = 60 ÷ 5/4.
Step 3: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: 60 × 4/5 = 48 km/h.
Answer: 48 km/h.
Similar example: 150 km in 2 h 30 min: time = 5/2 h, speed = 150 × 2/5 = 60 km/h.
Tip: Never write 1 h 15 min as 1.15. Use 1 + 15/60 = 1.25.

questions.text: Find the value of x for which the matrix [x 3; 4 6] is singular.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A matrix is singular when its determinant is zero. For [a b; c d], the determinant = ad − bc.
Step 1: The matrix is [x 3; 4 6]. Determinant = x × 6 − 3 × 4 = 6x − 12.
Step 2: Set the determinant to zero: 6x − 12 = 0.
Step 3: 6x = 12, so x = 12/6 = 2.
Answer: x = 2.
Similar example: Matrix [x 4; 3 6] is singular when 6x − 12 = 0, so x = 2.
Tip: Singular means no inverse, which happens when the determinant is 0.

questions.text: If log₁₀2 = 0.3010 and log₁₀3 = 0.4771, find log₁₀(48).
questions.explanation:
Concept: Laws of logarithms: log(xy) = log x + log y, and log(xⁿ) = n log x. Write the number using only the primes 2 and 3.
Step 1: Break 48 into factors of 2 and 3: 48 = 2⁴ × 3.
Step 2: Use the product and power laws: log 48 = 4 × log 2 + 1 × log 3.
Step 3: Substitute: 4(0.3010) + 1(0.4771) = 1.2040 + 0.4771.
Step 4: = 1.6811.
Answer: 1.6811.
Similar example: log 12 = log (2² × 3) = 2(0.3010) + 0.4771 = 1.0791.
Tip: Use prime factorisation. It turns any such number into a sum of the two given logs.

questions.text: Find the sum of the first 8 terms of the arithmetic progression 9, 11, 13, ...
questions.explanation:
Concept: An arithmetic progression (AP) goes up or down by the same amount each time, called the common difference d. The sum of the first n terms is Sₙ = n/2 × [2a + (n − 1)d], where a is the first term.
Step 1: Find a and d: a = 9, d = 11 − 9 = 2. Number of terms n = 8.
Step 2: Substitute: S = 8/2 × [2(9) + (8 − 1)(2)].
Step 3: Inside the bracket: 2(9) = 18, and (7)(2) = 14, so the bracket = 18 + 14 = 32.
Step 4: S = 8/2 × 32 = 128.
Answer: 128.
Similar example: Sum of the first 5 terms of 3, 7, 11, ...: S = 5/2 × [6 + 4(4)] = 5/2 × 22 = 55.
Tip: d is the second term minus the first. The bracket uses (n − 1), not n.

questions.text: From a point P on level ground 50 m from the foot B of a tower TB, the angle of elevation of the top T is 45°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The angle of elevation is the angle above the horizontal. In the right triangle TBP, tan(angle) = opposite/adjacent = TB/PB.
Step 1: Identify: adjacent side PB = 50 m (on the ground), opposite side TB = height.
Step 2: Write: tan 45° = TB/50, so TB = 50 × tan 45°.
Step 3: Use the exact value: tan 45° = 1.
Step 4: TB = 50 × 1 = 50 m.
Answer: 50 m.
Similar example: Distance 12 m, elevation 60°: height = 12 × √3 = 12√3 m.
Tip: Memorise: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

questions.text: Evaluate ∫ (3x² + 2x) dx from x = 0 to x = 2.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To integrate a power of x: ∫axⁿ dx = a xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1). For a definite integral, substitute the upper limit, then subtract the value at the lower limit.
Step 1: Integrate term by term: ∫(3x² + 2x) dx = 1x³ + 1x².
Step 2: Substitute x = 2: 1(2)³ + 1(2)² = 12.
Step 3: Substitute x = 0: the value is 0.
Step 4: Subtract: 12 − 0 = 12.
Answer: 12.
Similar example: ∫(4x + 3x²) dx from 0 to 2 = [2x² + x³] = 8 + 8 = 16.
Tip: Add 1 to the power and divide by the new power. No '+ C' is needed for definite integrals.

questions.text: Find the gradient of the curve y = 4x³ − 5x at x = 3.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The gradient of a curve at a point is the value of the derivative dy/dx at that point. First differentiate, then substitute the x-value.
Step 1: Differentiate: y = 4x³ − 5x, so dy/dx = 12x² − 5.
Step 2: Substitute x = 3: 12(3)² − 5.
Step 3: Evaluate: 108 − 5 = 103.
Answer: 103.
Similar example: Gradient of y = x³ + 2x at x = 1: dy/dx = 3x² + 2 = 5.
Tip: Differentiate first, substitute after. Never substitute into y first.

questions.text: Find the LCM of 4, 6 and 9.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The LCM (lowest common multiple) is the smallest number that every given number divides into exactly. Use prime factors: take each prime at its highest power.
Step 1: Write each number as a product of primes: 4 = 2²; 6 = 2 × 3; 9 = 3².
Step 2: Take the highest power of each prime that appears: 2² × 3².
Step 3: Multiply: 2² × 3² = 36.
Step 4: Check: 36 ÷ 4 = 9, 36 ÷ 6 = 6, 36 ÷ 9 = 4. All are whole numbers.
Answer: 36.
Similar example: LCM of 4, 6 and 10: 4 = 2², 6 = 2 × 3, 10 = 2 × 5, so LCM = 2² × 3 × 5 = 60.
Tip: LCM must be at least as big as the largest number. Do not just multiply all the numbers, that gives a common multiple but not the lowest.

questions.text: Two fair dice are thrown together. Find the probability that the sum is 5.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Probability = (number of favourable outcomes) ÷ (total number of outcomes). Two dice give 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes.
Step 1: Total outcomes = 6 × 6 = 36.
Step 2: List the pairs that add up to 5: (1,4), (2,3), (3,2), (4,1). That is 4 outcomes.
Step 3: P(sum = 5) = 4/36 = 1/9.
Answer: 1/9.
Similar example: Probability that the sum is 7: pairs (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) = 6, so 6/36 = 1/6.
Tip: List pairs in order, (1,4) and (4,1) are different outcomes.

questions.text: Simplify 1/6 + 1 − 1.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To add or subtract fractions, they must have the same denominator. Change every term to equivalent fractions with the LCM of the denominators.
Step 1: Find the LCM of the denominators 6, 1, 1: LCM = 6.
Step 2: Convert each term: 1/6 = 1/6; 1 = 6/6; 1 = 6/6.
Step 3: Combine the numerators and keep the denominator: (1 + 6 − 6)/6 = 1/6.
Answer: 1/6.
Similar example: 1/2 + 1/3 − 1/6: LCM = 6, so 3/6 + 2/6 − 1/6 = 4/6 = 2/3.
Tip: Never add or subtract the denominators. A whole number such as 2 is just 2/1.

questions.text: A number is increased by 20% to give 240. Find the number.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A percentage increase means the new value is (100 + p)% of the original. So the original is found by dividing the new value by (1 + p/100).
Step 1: Let the original number be N. Increasing by 20% gives 120% of N.
Step 2: So N × 120/100 = 240.
Step 3: N = 240 × 100/120 = 200.
Step 4: Check: 200 × 120/100 = 240. Correct.
Answer: 200.
Similar example: A number increased by 10% gives 220. N = 220 × 100/110 = 200.
Tip: Common mistake: taking 20% of 240 and subtracting. The 20% is of the original number, not of the new one.

questions.text: In the isosceles triangle shown, AB = AC and each base angle is 65°. Find the angle at the vertex A.
questions.explanation:
Concept: In an isosceles triangle, the two sides AB and AC are equal, so the angles opposite them (the base angles at B and C) are equal. The three angles of any triangle add up to 180°.
Step 1: Base angles: B = C = 65°.
Step 2: Add them: 65° + 65° = 130°.
Step 3: Angle at A = 180° − 130° = 50°.
Answer: 50°.
Similar example: Base angles of 50° each: A = 180 − 100 = 80°.
Tip: Do not stop at 2 × base angle. Subtract from 180° to get the vertex angle.

questions.text: The sector shown has radius 21 cm and angle 90°. Find the length of its arc. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
Concept: The arc is part of the circumference. Arc length = (θ/360) × 2πr.
Step 1: Write the fraction of the circle: 90/360 = 1/4.
Step 2: Find the full circumference: 2πr = 2 × (22/7) × 21 = 132 cm.
Step 3: Multiply: 1/4 × 132 = 33 cm.
Answer: 33 cm.
Similar example: Radius 7 cm, angle 60°: (60/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 7 = (1/6) × 44 = 22/3 cm.
Tip: Arc length uses 2πr (circumference). Sector area uses πr². Do not mix them up.

questions.text: Evaluate 1100₂ + 110₂.
questions.explanation:
Concept: To add numbers in base two, the easiest way is: convert both to base ten, add, then convert the sum back to base two.
Step 1: 1100₂ = 12 in base ten.
Step 2: 110₂ = 6 in base ten.
Step 3: Add: 12 + 6 = 18.
Step 4: Convert back: 18 ÷ 2 = 9 r 0, 9 ÷ 2 = 4 r 1, 4 ÷ 2 = 2 r 0, 2 ÷ 2 = 1 r 0, 1 ÷ 2 = 0 r 1. Reading the remainders upwards gives 10010₂.
Answer: 10010₂.
Similar example: Evaluate 101₂ + 11₂: 5 + 3 = 8, and 8 = 1000₂.
Tip: In base 2: 1 + 1 = 10 (write 0, carry 1). Use this to check by direct column addition.

questions.text: In the right-angled triangle ABC shown, find sin θ.
questions.explanation:
